questions.question: On a four-lane road, you do not need to stop for a stopped school bus if you are traveling in the opposite direction.
questions.explanation: On a highway with four or more lanes, you only stop for a school bus if you are traveling behind it. Always drive carefully near children.

questions.question: When approaching an intersection with no traffic lights or stop signs, a driver should:

options.text: Keep your speed and drive through.
Stop, look both ways, and then drive.
Let all other drivers go first.
Be ready to stop if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop if needed.
questions.explanation: At an intersection with no traffic control, yield to vehicles coming from the right. Always be ready to stop to avoid a crash. Remove your foot from the gas, cover the brake, and check left, right, and left again.

questions.question: On a two-lane road with a solid yellow line on your side, you can pass another vehicle.
questions.explanation: You can only pass when the broken yellow line is on your side of the centerline. A solid yellow line on your side means you cannot pass.

questions.question: When you reach a railroad crossing with no flashing lights or gates, you should:

options.text: Cross quickly as fast as you can.
Be ready to stop for any train.
Speed up to beat any trains.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop for any train.
questions.explanation: Always be ready to stop for trains before crossing the tracks, especially if there are no lights or gates. Only cross when there is room for your entire vehicle on the other side. Do not shift gears while crossing because your car might stall.

questions.question: For a driver age 21 or older, it is illegal to drive with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of:
questions.explanation: Drivers age 21 and older cannot drive with a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher. Driving under the influence of alcohol is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: If a cyclist is in your lane and you want to pass, you should:

options.text: Pass the cyclist like you would any other vehicle.
Tap your horn softly to warn them.
Wait until the opposite lane is clear, then change lanes to pass.

questions.explanation: Bicycles are vehicles and should be treated like any other vehicle. Use your horn softly to get their attention—a loud horn can startle them and cause a crash. Change lanes to pass safely. Never squeeze past a cyclist in a narrow lane.

questions.question: If an oncoming driver does not dim their headlights, you should:

options.text: Look at the center of the road.
Look to the right side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look to the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: Look to the right side of the road to avoid being blinded by their bright lights. This helps you see the road and stay in your lane. Do not use your bright lights in return.

questions.question: When turning left onto a one-way street, you should complete the turn into:

options.text: The lane closest to where you came from.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane closest to where you came from.
questions.explanation: Always turn into the lane closest to your previous lane. This is the safest way to turn.

questions.question: When you see a flashing yellow light at an intersection, you should:

options.text: Yield to all traffic before crossing.
Stop, then cross when it is safe.

questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down to a safe speed and cross the intersection with caution.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, you should move back to the right lane when:

options.text: You are one car length ahead of the other vehicle.
You can see both headlights of the other vehicle in your rearview mirror.
You are 50 feet ahead of the other vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can see both headlights of the other vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Only move back when you have enough space between you and the vehicle you passed. When you see both of their headlights in your rearview mirror, it is safe to return to the right lane.

questions.question: You turn onto a two-lane road with a broken yellow line down the middle. What does this tell you?

options.text: Traffic moves in one direction only.
You must stay left of the broken yellow lines.

questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. A broken yellow line means you can cross it to pass slower vehicles when it is safe.

questions.question: You must not drive faster than:

options.text: A speed that is safe and reasonable.
A speed that matches current conditions.

questions.explanation: You must follow the speed limit and drive at a safe, reasonable speed for the conditions. Consider traffic, pedestrians, weather, road quality, and light when choosing your speed.

questions.question: You must give the right-of-way to pedestrians who are:
questions.explanation: Yield to pedestrians crossing the street in marked or unmarked crosswalks. For safety, always yield to anyone crossing any street.

questions.question: You drive on a four-lane highway and see a school bus stopped across the road with red lights flashing. You:

options.text: Can pass only if a pedestrian signals that it is safe.
Can pass because you do not need to stop.
Must turn on your emergency flashers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can pass because you do not need to stop.
questions.explanation: On a four-lane highway, you only need to stop for a school bus if you are behind it. If the bus is on the opposite side, you may pass.

questions.question: Your license can be suspended if you are under 21 and your blood alcohol level is:
questions.explanation: Anyone under 21 cannot drive with any alcohol in their system. Any trace of alcohol will result in serious penalties, including a two-year license suspension.

questions.question: A solid white line on the road's right edge angles toward the center. This means:

options.text: You are near a construction area.
You will have to turn left soon.

questions.explanation: A solid edge line marks the boundary between the travel lane and the shoulder. When the line angles toward the center, it means the road is getting narrower ahead.

questions.question: It is illegal for a car to share a lane with a motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have the right to use an entire lane. Two motorcycles may share a lane, but a car should never share a lane with a motorcycle.

questions.question: A work zone:

options.text: Is marked with black and white signs.
Does not require you to slow down or pay extra attention.

questions.explanation: Work zones may be stationary or moving, such as with striping, mowing, or snow removal vehicles. Orange signs with black lettering mark work zones. Always slow down and stay alert in work zones.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs alert you to conditions ahead. This sign warns you that traffic signals are at the next intersection.

questions.question: A vehicle suddenly cuts in front of you, creating a hazard. What should you do first?

options.text: Honk your horn and brake hard.

questions.explanation: If a vehicle cuts in front of you, release the accelerator. This creates space between your vehicle and the other vehicle without requiring hard braking or swerving.

questions.question: Your vehicle does not have anti-lock brakes. You need to stop quickly. What should you do?

options.text: Press and hold the brake pedal down.

questions.explanation: Pumping the brakes is the best way to stop in an emergency. Your car will stop quickly and you can still steer.

questions.question: Your vehicle's wheels leave the pavement. What should you do first?

options.text: Turn the front wheels slightly left to get back onto the road.
Hold the steering wheel firmly, release the gas pedal, and gently apply the brakes.
Apply the brakes and turn the front wheels sharply to the left.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the steering wheel firmly, release the gas pedal, and gently apply the brakes.
questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel firmly, release the gas pedal, and gently apply the brakes. Let your speed slow down. Then check traffic and safely merge back onto the road. Do not turn the wheel sharply, as this can cause you to lose control or go into other lanes.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: Keep at least a three- to four-second gap between your vehicle and the one in front under normal driving.
As your speed increases, you should decrease your following distance.
Following distance is only important on snow and ice.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep at least a three- to four-second gap between your vehicle and the one in front under normal driving.
questions.explanation: Always keep a three- to four-second gap between your vehicle and the one in front of you on any road under normal conditions. Increase this gap in bad weather or heavy traffic.

questions.question: You reach an uncontrolled intersection at the same time as vehicles on your right and left. What should you do?

options.text: Give the right-of-way to the vehicle on your left.
Give the right-of-way to the vehicle on your right.
Wait until the intersection is clear before proceeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give the right-of-way to the vehicle on your right.
questions.explanation: At an uncontrolled intersection when vehicles arrive at the same time, the vehicle on the right has the right-of-way. Other vehicles then proceed in the order they arrived.

questions.question: You are driving in the center lane of an expressway. Vehicles pass you on both sides. What should you do?
questions.explanation: On roads with four or more lanes, use the right lanes unless you are passing or turning left. On interstate highways, use the right lane if you are driving slower than traffic flow.

questions.question: You are driving on a busy street and your gas pedal gets stuck open. What should you do?

options.text: Turn off the ignition carefully without locking the steering wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off the ignition carefully without locking the steering wheel.
questions.explanation: Turn off the ignition by moving the key only far enough to stop the engine. Do not turn it far enough to lock the steering wheel. Then apply the brakes and pull off the road to a safe area.

questions.question: A fire engine is following you on a two-lane street with no emergency signals on. What should you do?

options.text: Stop as quickly as you can.
Speed up to get out of its way.
Slow down, move far to the right, and stop.

questions.explanation: If an emergency vehicle is following you but has no siren or flashing lights on, you do not need to pull over. Drive normally.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. They tell you about upcoming road conditions and hazards. This sign warns that a sharp turn is coming and you should reduce your speed.

questions.question: When may you park or stop on the freeway shoulder?

options.text: As long as you turn on your four-way flashers.
If your vehicle is completely off the road.
If you need to check a map for directions.

questions.explanation: You cannot park on a freeway shoulder except in an emergency.

questions.question: You are parking uphill on a road with no curb. Which way should you turn your front wheels?

options.text: Right, toward the side of the road
Left, toward the center of the road

questions.correctAnswerText: Right, toward the side of the road
questions.explanation: When parking uphill or downhill on a road with no curb, turn your wheels so your vehicle rolls away from the center of the road if the brakes fail.
